        - heading "Understand Local and Global Extrema" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Extrema are maximum or minimum values, either near a point or over the whole domain. You can learn Local and Global Extrema by trying one small example instead of long theory.

      - article:
        - heading "FORMULA & RULE" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Let f be continuous on a closed interval [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b).
        - paragraph: • Absolute extrema exist on [a,b].
        - paragraph: • Local extrema can occur at critical points where f′(c)=0 or DNE.
        - paragraph: • Also check endpoints a and b.
        - complementary: "☆ Rule: Compare f(a), f(b) and f(c) at all critical points c in (a,b)."
      - article:
        - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Find all extrema of f(x)=−2x²+4x+1 on [−5,5].
        - paragraph: 1. f′(x)=−4x+4=0 ⇒ x=1
        - paragraph: "2. Evaluate:"
        - paragraph:

          - text: • f(−5)=−69
          - text: • f(5)=−29
        - paragraph: 3. Compare values.
        - status:
          - text: "Absolute maximum: 3 at x=1"
          - text: "Absolute minimum: −69 at x=−5"
          - text: "Local maximum: 3 at x=1"
      - article:
        - heading "⚠ MISCONCEPTION ALERT" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Don't confuse local and global!
        - list:
          - listitem: The highest local point is not always the global maximum.
          - listitem: Always compare values at endpoints and critical points.
